## Read this before acting on any row

**Static analysis cannot determine whether a flagged API degrades silently, throws, or
works.** WebKit is closed-source, and reading wry's source only shows what Rust *asked*
WebKit to do — not what WebKit did. This project has already seen all three behaviours from
APIs that look identical in source: `navigator.clipboard.writeText` resolves and writes
nothing, `queryLocalFonts` throws, and `delete_cookie()` resolves having deleted nothing.

Every row below is therefore **a candidate for a future targeted spike, not a defect
claim.** `UNVERIFIED-LIVE` means *nobody has watched this one* — a statement about our
evidence, not about the code. Resolving these inline is out of scope by construction; plan
28 requires `git diff --stat -- src/` to be empty for the commit that generated this file.

### Allowlist entries with no code reference

Recorded explicitly: absence is a result. An API that was remediated (clipboard) and one
that was never used look identical here, so the closing section distinguishes them.

- `navigator.clipboard` — no reference in scanned source. Chromium's async clipboard. Under WKWebView `writeText` RESOLVES without writing (observed, this project).
- `navigator.usb` — no reference in scanned source. WebUSB, Chromium-only. Absent in Safari/WKWebView.
- `navigator.serial` — no reference in scanned source. Web Serial, Chromium-only. Absent in Safari/WKWebView.
- `navigator.bluetooth` — no reference in scanned source. Web Bluetooth, Chromium-only. Absent in Safari/WKWebView.
- `showOpenFilePicker` — no reference in scanned source. File System Access API, Chromium-only. Absent in Safari/WKWebView.
- `showSaveFilePicker` — no reference in scanned source. File System Access API, Chromium-only. Absent in Safari/WKWebView.
- `document.fonts` — no reference in scanned source. CSS Font Loading. Basic FontFace is supported; `check`/`ready` timing and the FontFaceSet iteration surface differ in WebKit.
- `Notification.requestPermission` — no reference in scanned source. Permission model differs; WKWebView may resolve without ever prompting the user.
- `navigator.mediaDevices` — no reference in scanned source. getUserMedia/enumerateDevices gating differs materially in WebKit.
- `webkitSpeechRecognition` — no reference in scanned source. Prefixed Chromium API; not the WebKit-shipped surface.
- `navigator.storage` — no reference in scanned source. StorageManager estimate()/persist() differ in WebKit.
- `ResizeObserver` — no reference in scanned source. Supported, but WebKit's delivery timing differs -- listed because layout-timing assumptions are how F-10 hid for a whole gate cycle.

## The four known instances — calibration

What this tool would have caught versus what a human found by driving a UI. Three of the
four were found live; none was found by a scanner. That ratio is the honest measure of what
a static sweep is worth here.

| Instance | Runtime behaviour | Found by | Status after this cycle |
|----------|-------------------|----------|--------------------------|
| `navigator.clipboard.writeText` | Resolves without writing | Live gate (human) | CLOSED — replaced by `window.api.clipboardWriteText`; no code reference remains in `src/`. |
| `queryLocalFonts` | Throws | Live gate (human) | CLOSED — plan 27 extracted `queryLocalFontsSafe()`, which guards both failure shapes. |
| `delete_cookie()` (wry) | Resolves having deleted nothing | Live gate (human) | F-6 — see `34.4.1-LIVE-GATE-RERUN.md`; the shared Rust arm's bug hits every caller. |
| Login window title (process-level) | Assumed default Tauri behaviour, never spiked | Code review | Plan 24 wired `on_document_title_changed`; the live half is plan 29's to observe. |
